note: Historical event template DATA. Sources resolve against scenario sources[].

events.title: Wacht am Rhein: the German offensive begins
events.body: A 90-minute barrage from about 1,600 guns opens the German offensive along a 130 km front. Thick overcast, fog and snow keep Allied aircraft grounded. Skorzeny's 150th Panzer Brigade stands ready for Operation Greif.
events.effectsNote: Restates B10: overcast, fog and snow grounded Allied aircraft 16-22 Dec.

events.title: Peiper captures fuel at Büllingen; Malmedy massacre
events.body: Kampfgruppe Peiper seizes an American fuel depot at Büllingen and refuels its tanks; later at Malmedy crossroads at least 84 American prisoners are killed.
effectHints: German fuel relief if Büllingen depot captured

events.title: Peiper takes Stavelot; Trois-Ponts bridge blown
events.body: Peiper's column takes Stavelot, but US engineers blow the bridge at Trois-Ponts. Stoumont falls the next day.

events.title: Montgomery orders the Meuse bridges held
events.body: Montgomery orders the Meuse bridges at Givet, Dinant and Namur held; XXX Corps is ordered to hold the Meuse as a stop-line and the 29th Armoured Brigade moves to the Namur-Dinant sector. The 101st Airborne reaches Bastogne.

events.title: Schnee Eifel surrender
events.body: About 7,000 American soldiers of the 106th Division surrender on the Schnee Eifel, the largest US defeat in the European Theater.

events.title: Bastogne cut off; Montgomery takes the northern shoulder
events.body: The roads into Bastogne are cut and the 101st Airborne is surrounded. Eisenhower places the US First and Ninth Armies under Montgomery.

events.title: St. Vith evacuated
events.body: On Montgomery's orders Brig. Gen. Clarke withdraws from St. Vith after delaying the German timetable.

events.title: "Nuts!"
events.body: The Germans demand the surrender of Bastogne. McAuliffe replies "NUTS!"

events.title: The weather clears
events.body: The skies clear and much colder air arrives. Allied air attacks begin and 241 transport aircraft drop supplies to Bastogne; Peiper breaks out from La Gleize.
events.effectsNote: Restates B02/B10: weather cleared on 23 Dec. The 3-day duration is a game-scale choice; sources disagree on when clear weather ended.

events.title: High-water mark at Foy-Notre-Dame
events.body: The US 2nd Armored Division stops the German advance at Foy-Notre-Dame, short of the Meuse at Dinant. Manteuffel asks for a halt; Hitler refuses.

events.title: Bastogne relieved
events.body: Company D, 37th Tank Battalion, 4th Armored Division reaches Bastogne from the south, ending the siege. The German push to the Meuse is effectively over by 27 December.

events.title: Operation Bodenplatte
events.body: The Luftwaffe attacks Allied airfields; about 465 Allied aircraft are destroyed or damaged but the Luftwaffe loses 277 aircraft and is largely ineffective for the rest of the war.

events.title: Montgomery's counter-offensive begins
events.body: The northern counter-offensive begins; Hitler agrees on 7/8 January to withdraw gradually from the tip of the salient.

events.title: First and Third Armies link up at Houffalize
events.body: The Third and First Armies link up with the capture of Houffalize; First Army returns to 12th Army Group command.

events.title: Sixth Panzer Army cedes its sector
events.body: Sixth Panzer Army cedes its sector to Fifth Panzer Army.

events.title: The Ardennes battle ends
events.body: The battle is considered ended on 25 January (the infobox of the primary source gives 28 January).
